articleTitle: Accelerated performance degradation test and analysis of high-temperature strain gauges
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: With the extension of the service time of the structure and the worse service temperature conditions, the drift problem of hightemperature strain gauges gradually becomes prominent. This research aims to address the issue of the drift of measurement results because of the performance degradation of high-temperature strain gauges, and investigate the drift law under different temperatures considering complex service environments. In this paper, a combination of experimental research and theoretical analysis is utilized to design and conduct the accelerated performance degradation test on high-temperature strain gauges. Based on the result of the test, an accelerated performance degradation model is developed using the Wiener process and Arrhenius model. Finally, estimation curves for the average value and percentile value of the performance parameters of the hightemperature strain gauges are obtained, which demonstrates that the established accelerated performance degradation model can reasonably describe the degradation law. Additionally, the established accelerated performance degradation model enables effective analysis and compensation of gauge drift at any temperature.

articleTitle: Characterization of a new fatigue test bench for pulsed high frequency reliability testing of hydraulic components
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Hydraulic components are under huge hydraulic pressure for a long time, so they need to be tested for high cycle fatigue reliability by hydraulic pulse fatigue testing. However, the control valve of the conventional hydraulic pulse fatigue test bench usually uses a servo valve. And the conventional servo valve's low-frequency response will limit the hydraulic pulse fatigue test bench's high-frequency output and increase the fatigue test's cycle time. An innovative configuration of a high-speed reversing valve is proposed to solve this problem. The valve adopts a two-stage configuration. The pilot stage adopts the form of a rotary valve to realize the speed amplification, and the main stage adopts the form of a slide valve for power amplification. The driving of the main spool is realized through the alternate switching of the pilot stage oil port. In this paper, the working principle is described, the mathematical model is built and the AMESim simulation analysis verifies its feasibility. The results show that the test bench can output high frequency excitation force.

articleTitle: Diagnosis method of abnormal fluctuation of CPU usage based on iForest-Bi-LSTM
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Abnormal fluctuation diagnosis plays a vital role in the security of large-scale systems, which is an important method to maintain the smooth operation of the system and improve the troubleshooting efficiency. When the CPU fluctuates abnormally, the performance of the application process in the system will be affected. And if the abnormality continues, it will cause a crashing impact. For that reason, it is necessary to detect the abnormal phenomenon early. According to the fluctuation characteristics of CPU usage series, a fluctuation prediction model based on Isolation Forest (iForest) and Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) is constructed, and the normal fluctuation range of the sequence is further calculated based on the sample size and confidence interval to realize the abnormal diagnosis of the monitoring data. The relevant results on four different distribution datasets show that the iForest-Bi-LSTM prediction model has the lowest fitting error, the highest prediction accuracy, and stronger robustness and applicability compared with a single deep learning model and a time series prediction model with integrated anomaly detection. Eventually, the iForest-Bi-LSTM model based on historical samples is introduced into the complex O&M system of the data center, which can adapt the data distribution characteristics, calculate the sequence fluctuation interval, and complete the abnormal diagnosis of monitoring data within milliseconds.

articleTitle: A small sample reliability assessment method based on Bayesian theory
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In addressing the specific challenges associated with the small sample size and extended lifespan of critical equipment, this paper proposes a small sample reliability assessment method grounded in Bayesian theory. The underlying principle of the Bayesian method is elucidated, along with the processes for acquiring the prior distribution and determining the posterior distribution. Building on this framework, an evaluation process for small sub-samples based on Bayesian theory is introduced. The model is then applied to the life test data of a particular product. The findings demonstrate that the reliability assessment leveraging Bayesian methodology can effectively enhance the reliability of small sample products upon the incorporation of prior information. This approach ameliorates issues commonly encountered in classical methods, such as overly low assessment results, stark inconsistencies with empirical understanding, and inaccuracies in evaluation.

articleTitle: Fatigue strength optimization of planetary gear rim for wind power gearbox
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: During the operation of a 1.5MW wind turbine gearbox, fatigue failure in the planetary gears has been attributed to the occurrence of outer ring deformation within the planet wheel bearing and sliding along the planet wheel hole. This study employs theoretical calculations and finite element analysis to investigate the impact of planetary wheel flange thickness on stress distribution within the planetary gear body. Through structural optimization of the flange, the radial deformation of the planetary wheel bearing hole during operation is mitigated, thereby enhancing the fatigue resistance of the planetary wheel flange. By effectively reducing and preventing relative sliding between the planetary wheel bearing and the planet wheel hole, this research establishes a robust theoretical foundation for ensuring the dependable operation of the gearbox's planetary gears.

articleTitle: A novel parameter estimation method for lognormal and birnbaum-saunders distributions on heavily censored data
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Lifetime data collected from field are often heavily censored. For such data, it has been concluded that total-time-on-test-based mean life estimator considerably overestimates mean time to failure (MTTF) and the maximum likelihood estimates (MLEs) of distribution parameters are not stable. Several novel methods with satisfactory accuracy have been proposed to estimate the MTTF and distribution parameters on heavily censored data. One of these methods is based on the conjecture: fitting a heavilycensored dataset to a single-parameter nearly-symmetric distribution can yield a fairly accurate MLE of MTTF. In this paper, we extend this conjecture to the case of 2-parameter symmetric distribution. The normal and logistic distributions, whose density functions are symmetric, are considered, and 24 heavily censored datasets are randomly generated from these two distributions with different parameter combinations. For these datasets, it is shown that the average of relative errors of MLEs of MTTF is 9.64%. Thus, the conjecture is validated. Based on the conjecture, a novel parameter estimation method for the lognormal and Birnbaum-Saunders distributions on heavily censored data is proposed and illustrated by a real-world example.

articleTitle: A LSTM-based Monte Carlo quantile regression method for satellite temperature prediction and data uncertainty quantification
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Satellite on-orbit temperature data analysis is of great importance for improving satellite reliability and executing in-time health management. Due to the time series property of the on-orbit temperature data, the Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network is a major method to solve the future temperature prediction problem. However, the data uncertainty caused by temperature noise is not considered in the traditional LSTM. To address this problem and improve prediction accuracy, a LSTM-based Monte Carlo Quantile Regression method (LSTM-MCQR) is proposed in this paper. On one hand, quantile levels sampled randomly from the uniform distribution are integrated with the time serial data as the input of the LSTM network in each training epoch. On the other hand, the data uncertainty is quantified through the trained model by sampling quantile levels again during the prediction process. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by an actual engineering case. Results demonstrate that a more accurate predicted temperature with the quantified uncertainty can be acquired, which is conducive to further reliability analysis.

articleTitle: Research on fault diagnosis of ship equipment based on vibration signal
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Currently, the mainstream method to monitor the health status of ship pump equipment is to evaluate its health status according to its health state values such as pressure and temperature. However, there is a lack of methods for fault diagnosis based on vibration signals of pump equipment. The vibration signals of the pump attempt to be used in the paper to monitor the health by referencing the bearing-based fault diagnosis method. A classification model is constructed by using wavelet transformation and support vector machines (SVM) to achieve fault diagnosis of the equipment. Firstly, wavelet transformation is used to denoise the vibration data and perform feature extraction. Then, in order to improve the model accuracy, the models are trained separately for different measuring points. Finally, the final diagnosis results are obtained by voting based on all classification results, and diagnosis results as well as maintenance suggestions are given accordingly. The accuracy test results of the final model show that the classification accuracy of the model for pump equipment vibration signals reaches 100%, which has practical application value.

articleTitle: A predictive maintenance model for degrading systems operating under performance-based contracting
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Performance-based contracting (PBC) is a novel service system that provides the suppliers with payment and incentives, thereby motivating them to improve system performance (reliability and availability, etc.) through effective maintenance actions. This paper proposes a new predictive maintenance model for deteriorating systems operating in the PBC environment. The inspection-based maintenance decision relies on the prognostic information given the current health state of the system. From the perspective of the service supplier, the cost rate for maintaining the contracted system is evaluated based on semiregenerative properties. The payment to the supplier for the maintenance service, is directly dependent on the resulting system performance, which is measured by the average system availability over the contract period. The optimization of the inspection interval and the conditional reliability threshold of the system aims to trigger proactive maintenance interventions while maximizing the profit rate for the service supplier. The developed predictive maintenance model's applicability is validated through a numerical example and sensitivity analysis involving several key parameters.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation model of parking lot mobile payment system considering function upgradation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Within the software industry, the pace of software upgrades remains swift due to fierce market competition and rapidly evolving requirements. The fluctuating composition of development teams poses challenges in testing upgraded software. Despite this, limited attention has been devoted to testing strategies and reliability estimation for upgraded software systems, leveraging past testing data. Therefore, it is important and necessary to develop an effective testing strategy in order to ensure the product quality. In this paper, an upgradation software testing strategy adapted to requirements change will be proposed combined with the software development process of Parking Lot Mobile Payment System (PLMPS). In this approach, the testing information of the pre-versions and software functional structure will be fully used in upgradation software testing. Moreover, an upgradation software reliability model can be constructed based on proposed testing strategy. The proposed reliability model also can be applied to multi upgradation software systems. Furthermore, the proposed approach can help managers and developers generate testing cases and predict software reliability. A numerical example based on simulation data is given to illustrate its application in the modeling process.

articleTitle: Research on physical modeling method for friction and wear failure of slotted contact parts
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Electrical connectors are essential components in electrical systems. During their usage, frictional wear can occur between the pin and socket of the contact components. Excessive contact resistance resulting from this phenomenon can lead to system failure, emphasizing the critical importance of ensuring the stability of the contact component's performance. In this study, the commonly used slotted contact component was selected, and its mechanical characteristics were initially analyzed to determine the required parameters for experimentation. Subsequently, vibration tests under different vibration conditions were conducted on the contact component at room temperature, revealing the wear patterns of the contact component under various vibration conditions. Finally, a physical model for the failure of frictional wear was established for the selected contact component model based on the parameters obtained from the experiments.

articleTitle: Research of safety design method of solid rocket test plant
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The solid rocket test facility situated at the aerospace launch center is classified as a hazardous structure. In the event of an explosion, the repercussions can be extremely grave. The safety design content and design methods that should be focused on are proposed in this paper, and safety design of solid rocket test plants is researched. The approach encompasses various steps, such as plant site selection, safety area delineation, building configuration, and structural choice, implementation of electrical explosion-proof measures, and fire protection design. Furthermore, design examples are provided to offer guidance to pertinent designers.

articleTitle: Bearing misalignment identification by adaptive time frequency modal decomposition under time-varying speed operating condition
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: To detect the misalignment of bearings during dynamically changing operational conditions, A new and innovative approach is introduced for adaptive time-frequency modal decomposition (TFMD). The optimization of window width for TFMD was carried out, then the nonlinear relationship between window width and output was studied to obtain the adaptive TFMD. To verify the TFMD, the experiment was conducted on bearing misalignment faults, and adaptive TFMD was used to perform modal decomposition and order analysis on the data. By calculating the energy ratio of each order, fault characteristics of the vibration signal were analyzed. The experimental results demonstrate that TFMD enhances the signal-to-noise ratio of modal decomposition and exhibits effective diagnostic capabilities for identifying misalignment faults. The proposed method will become a worthwhile method for non-stationary signal analysis and fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Investigating regional effects of random inputs for multivariate outputs with generalized variance
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Many computational models used in structural design produce multivariate outputs. This paper aims at quantifying how the subranges of model input variables affect the uncertainty of compositive multivariate outputs. Generalized variance in multivariate statistical theory is firstly introduced to describe the uncertainties of multivariate outputs. From geometric perspective, it is clear that the generalized variance represents both uncertainties of a single output and the correlations between two different outputs. The generalized variance ratio function is then defined to investigate the effect on the multivariate outputs when the uncertainty of one or a set of input variables are reduced to their subranges. Two efficient computational procedures called single-loop Monte Carlo simulation and sparse grid integration are developed to calculate the proposed regional sensitivity index. At last, by applying the proposed method to two typical cases, it is illustrated in detail about how to use the information provided by the developed regional sensitivity theory.

articleTitle: Research on damage identification of wind turbine blade based on LSTM-CNN
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Cracks are the main mode of wind turbine blade faults. In order to accurately determine the extent of blade crack damage, a damage recognition model based on LSTM-CNN is proposed. Data sets were collected through acoustic emission technology. For one-dimensional signals, a convolutional neural network architecture was designed, and an improved method of pre-staging the fully connected layer was proposed. The LeakyReLU and ReLU functions were applied to adjust the data format, and the Dropout value was set to avoid overfitting. The classification was output in a convolutional form through layer transmission. In addition, The LSTM network was added to the CNN to optimize the model and enhance the feature extraction capability of time series data correlation. The recognition accuracy of the final LSTM-CNN network model was 98.8%, which is 2.0% higher than the CNN structure. This proposed model has a great value to be applied into the wind turbine blade damage recognition work.

articleTitle: Bearing intelligent fault diagnosis method based on MCNN-BiLSTM-SVM
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) adopts the softmax function as a classifier, which has problems of overflow and underflow. To address this issue, CNN and bi-directional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) are combined with multi-scales (MCNN-BiLSTM) as the feature extractor to improve feature extraction capability, and then support vector machine (SVM) is employed as the classifier to improve classification performance. Thus, an intelligent fault diagnosis method combined with MCNN-BiLSTM and SVM (MCNN-BiLSTM-SVM) is proposed. The wavelet threshold denoising algorithm is adopted for signal preprocessing. Transfer learning is used in MCNN-BiLSTM-SVM for different conditions. According to the bearing fault diagnosis experiments, the proposed MCNN-BiLSTM-SVM fault diagnosis method has higher diagnostic accuracy, stronger anti-noise performance and better stability under different conditions than other diagnostic methods.

articleTitle: Measuring risk based on safety performance
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Operation safety is very important for the civil aviation industry. Traditional methods for risk assessment primarily are focused on accidents or incidents, however researchers have recently paid more attentions to safety performance management. Although most studies are tended to establish safety performance indicators to provide the meaningful inputs for senior management decision-making, there is little research on comprehensive multi-level risk assessment based on safety performance indicator system. For that reason, this paper aims to propose a practical risk assessment framework for civil aviation organizations. On the basis of Heinrich's Law, weights for company-level controlling indicator, company-level monitoring indicator, departmentlevel controlling indicator and department-level monitoring indicator are assigned by operation and safety management experts. Safety performance indicator system of an airport and its safety supervision department have also been defined by different method, such as event tree analysis, failure mode and effects analysis, Bowtie, fault tree analysis, fishbone diagram analysis, SHELL model, etc. Besides, the proposed comprehensive risk assessment model is verified by the actual collected operation data of the airport and its safety supervision department.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of high-speed train braking system based on graph diffusion convolution model
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to fault diagnosis in high-speed train braking systems through the integration of graph neural networks and causality analysis. Specifically, a fault diagnosis model is formulated based on a graph diffusion model. Cyclic causality is extracted from the data using Function Causality Inference (FCI), leading to the construction of a causality graph. Subsequently, the adjacency matrix is transformed into a diffusion transfer matrix using the graph diffusion model, enabling the aggregation of higher-order information. A graph classification model, employing Graph Attention Networks (GAT), is then established to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed fault diagnosis model. Through comprehensive comparative analysis, the performance enhancement of the high-speed train fault classifier achieved by this approach is verified. The results underscore that our fault diagnosis model not only enhances the interpretability and reasoning capabilities of cyclic causality, but also adeptly captures the high-dimensional structural information inherent in the graph. This amalgamation leads to a more precise and pragmatic fault diagnosis model.

articleTitle: Multi-strategy fusion improved grey wolf algorithm for complex parts point cloud data registration
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: To address the challenges of low accuracy and high computational time in 3D point cloud registration, various point cloud registration algorithms have been proposed in recent years. Among these, the gray wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm has gained significant attention for its effectiveness in handling complex optimization problems. However, traditional GWO has limitations in terms of search efficiency and susceptibility to local optima. Therefore, this paper presents an improved point cloud registration method based on the GWO algorithm. The proposed method incorporates Logistic-Tent(L-T) chaotic mapping for population initialization to achieve a more uniform distribution within the search space. Additionally, a nonlinear control parameter strategy is introduced to balance the algorithm's local and global search capabilities. Furthermore, elite backward learning is integrated to enhance the quality of the algorithm's solutions. Finally, the Iterative Closest Points (ICP) algorithm is employed for fine registration. The registration experiments conducted on collected automotive body panel point cloud datasets validate the effectiveness and practicality of the improved algorithm, as demonstrated through comparative analysis with other algorithms.

articleTitle: Risk assessment of passenger flow dispersion in urban rail transit transfer stations
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Urban rail transit has become an important part of the urban public transportation system. The transfer station serves as the intersection of urban rail transit lines to entire urban rail transit lines as an interconnected network. Once the passenger flow at the transfer station is not well dispersed, it will adversely affect the several lines and even the entire line network. Therefore, it is of great significance to scientifically evaluate the passenger flow dispersion risk of the transfer station. In this paper, a datadriven method is proposed to analyse the characteristics of passenger flow (e.g., the moving speed of different groups). A set of passenger flow diversion evaluation indicators for rail transit transfer stations is established, including the passenger flow density, emergency evacuation time, station passenger facility saturation, transfer time, and average transfer distance. And the software of AnyLogic and STEPS are applied to simulate the evacuation process. By comparing the observation data with the simulation results, the simulation model is verified to show that the simulation results have a good agreement with the actual situation. A case study with focusing on transfer Station X is adapted to illustrate the feasibility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of horizontal machining center based on fuzzy FMECA
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The traditional FMECA method is used to analyze the reliability of horizontal machining centers. The obtained hazard degree results are often difficult to rank, due to the disadvantages of using the risk priority number to assess the hazard degree of the system, which is influenced by the subjective factors of the assessor. To assign weights among the three elements of risk, a hazard degree assessment method based on fuzzy theory is proposed in this article. The evaluation results are obtained by constructing a fuzzy evaluation matrix and a weight vector to obtain the hazard ranking of the failure modes. The results obtained by the conventional FMECA method are compared to those obtained by the fuzzy FMECA method, to find the components with the highest hazard level. By this method, the operational reliability of the systems can be improved.

articleTitle: An improved YOLOv5s algorithm for mechanical parts detection
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: YOLOv5s algorithm has made significant progress in object detection. However, it contains a large number of parameters, and its detection speed is low. To overcome the problem, an improved YOLOv5s algorithm is proposed. Firstly, ghost convolution and ghost bottleneck layers of the GhostNet are added to the convolution and bottleneck layers of the YOLOv5s algorithm. Secondly, a feature pyramid network is employed to continuously update the weights of the branches during training, which can fuse features of different resolutions. Finally, an Attention Mechanism is added to the backbone network to extract the deep features of mechanical parts. The experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm can more accurately and quickly identify mechanical parts.

articleTitle: Extended reliability modeling and simulation of multi-state production systems based on dynamic fault tree
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In order to cope with increasingly complex production tasks, the reliability requirements of some production systems are becoming increasingly high. During operation, the production systems are mostly multi-state in performance, mainly due to item failure or degradation in the system. As we all know, Dynamic Fault Tree is often used to evaluate the reliability of twostate systems, but it does not work for multi-state systems. Therefore, this paper extended the performance degradation logic gate model based on Dynamic Fault Tree and gave related simulation algorithms based on Monte Carlo sampling to calculate quantitative values for reliability such as Availability, MTBCF, MTTR, and so on. Finally, this article, taking production system D as an example, demonstrated the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: An adaptive modelling method based on infill strategy maximum entropy
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Instead of the real finite element model, the the approximate model can achieve a balance between calculation accuracy and computational cost, and computation efficiency can also be improved. There are two main ways to implement approximate Modelling: (1) Single step Modelling method; (2) Adaptive Modelling method. When constructing the approximate model, the single-step method employs one-time sampling to obtain sample points. If there are too many sample points, significant computational resources and costs are required for solving; conversely, too few points can lead to inaccuracy in the approximation. Consequently, the single-step method is not typically utilized. Acknowledging these limitations, this paper introduces a Support Vector Regression (SVR) adaptive modeling method, grounded in the infill strategy of maximum entropy. This approach augments the training sample with points of the highest entropy value and updates the approximation model, utilizing the entropy value of the sample to represent the model's error. To prevent over-sampling in any specific area, newly acquired sample points must also adhere to the principle of minimizing distance while maximizing coverage. The computational efficacy of this proposed method is substantiated through three numerical examples.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of a cabin door lock mechanism with two correlated function failure modes
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The present study focuses on how to accurately and efficiently estimate the reliability of lock mechanism with two correlated function failure modes. Taking an aircraft cabin door lock mechanism as the research object, a dynamic model is established in LMS Virtual. lab according to the analysis of the lock mechanism working principle. The main failure modes of the lock mechanism are determined to be seizure failure and kinematic accuracy failure. The influencing factors of the two failure modes are analyzed. Then, considering the correlation between the two failure modes, the weighted nonlinear response surface (WRSM) and Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) are used to analyze the reliability of the lock mechanism. Finally, the calculated result is compared with the direct MCS. The comparison shows that the error between our method and direct MCS is about 1%, which proves the rationality of our method. The calculation efficiency is greatly improved compared with the direct MCS. Meanwhile, the method can also be applied to the reliability analysis of other similar mechanisms.

articleTitle: Research on spring life prediction model and data processing method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Spring is a very common mechanical part, which has the functions of buffering, shock absorption, energy storage, motion control, positioning, and so on. The inherent reliability of basic components such as springs has a profound impact on the reliability of its affiliated products. Therefore, it is particularly important to study its degradation mechanism and law and predict its reliability index. In this paper, the principle of spring life prediction using the accelerated proportional degradation risk model and environmental action dynamics model is analyzed respectively, and the method of spring life prediction using the accelerated proportional degradation risk model is simulated and analyzed. The similarities and differences between the predicted results and the actual storage results were compared by example calculations and comparison with the results of natural storage.

articleTitle: Reliability allocation of CNC machine tools based on AHP-entropy weight method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The reliability allocation approach for NC machine tools heavily relies on expert assessments, making the outcomes susceptible to the expertise levels of the evaluators. This dependence results in issues such as subjectivity and a deficiency in objective information evaluation. To address these concerns, this paper introduces a novel reliability allocation methodology for numerical control machine tools. This method is grounded in the AHP-entropy weight technique. It takes expert opinions and objective factors into consideration and then allocates the reliability of the numerical control machine tool. Firstly, collecting subjective opinions of experts and fault data of similar products, establishing a reliability evaluation model of the CNC machine tool, and an evaluation system of the NC machine tool, which is based on fault frequency, fault influence degree, hazard, and complexity. Then, AHP is used to analyze the subjective weight of the expert opinion subsystem, and the entropy weight method is used to obtain the objective data subsystem weight. Finally, the comprehensive weight of each subsystem is obtained, and the reliability of the CNC machine tool is allocated.

articleTitle: A method for estimating the consumption of spare parts in electromechanical equipment considering maintenance time
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Spare parts are an important equipment maintenance resource, and the allocation quantity of spare parts can be used to measure the degree of maintenance support. Therefore, scientifically determining the consumption quantity of spare parts is of great practical significance for achieving precise support. This article takes electromechanical equipment with a Weibull distribution as the research object and proposes an estimation method that considers the average consumption of spare parts of maintenance time. The maintenance time is included in the different probability scenarios of the total consumption of each spare part for calculation, an example analysis is carried out. The method will be conducted to improve the accuracy of the evaluation of the average consumption of spare parts of electromechanical equipment and to provide practical engineering methods for scientifically carrying out many spare parts management work.

articleTitle: Impact reliability analysis of isolation system shock absorber
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: A reliability analysis study was conducted on the shock absorber used in a certain ship. Firstly, a multi-source uncertainty quantification model was established. Different forms of models are used to quantify the uncertainty of loads, geometric shapes, and material properties based on their characteristics. Then, combining Monte-Carlo method with BP neural network surrogate model, the relationship between input variables and output acceleration is established. Finally, based on the surrogate model, the response distribution and reliability of the shock absorber are obtained, which provides a reference for the subsequent structural analysis and optimization.

articleTitle: A motion precision reliability assessment method for quadrotor UAV by combining PCE and intelligent optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The application of the quadrotor UAV (unmanned aerial vehicles) is more and more extensive, the dynamic performance and motion precision are important index of quadrotor UAV. Uncertainties from the geometric parameters, material properties, and operation load, etc., will influence the dynamic performance and motion precision, therefore, it is required to estimate the motion precision of quadrotor UAV considering the effects of uncertainties. In this paper, the dynamic performance of quadrotor UAV under mixed uncertainties is investigated, and a motion precision reliability analysis method for quadrotor UAV by combining PCE (polynomial chaos expansions) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) method is developed. In this method, the dynamic performance of quadrotor UAV is analyzed considering the interval uncertainty from moment of inertia and random uncertainty from payload, the PSO method is employed to estimate the interval limits of the displacement. On this basis, the motion precision reliability estimation model is established by PCE at the maximal displacement error. The results from the proposed method and Monte Carlo (MC) simulation are compared, which proves the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Seismic autocorrelation: structure along the Bilby array and link to Marla line in central Australia
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Autocorrelation of the immediate coda of P waves provides an alternative to traditional receiver functions. Working at higher frequencies enhanced information can be extracted on the Moho surface. We show that the autocorrelation process is equivalent to a virtual point source at the surface, and this enables the extraction of local reflectivity. ACC (Auto-Correlogram Calculation in Seismology) software is used to process and analyze teleseismic P-wave coda recorded along the Bilby array aligned north to south and the Marla array aligned east to west in central Australia. Clear signals can be extracted for the Moho, mid lithospheric discontinuity (MLD), and the transition from the lithosphere to the asthenosphere (LAT), exploiting reflectivity estimates in different frequency bands (up to 5 Hz upper bound). The Moho of Bilby lies at 40 km or deeper, the MLD around 80-90 km depth, and the LAT between 130 and 180 km depth. A cross-check on the nature of the seismic structure is provided by the intersection with the dense Marla array (MAL) in an east-west direction near stations BL19 and BL20. Consistent reflectivity results are extracted in orthogonal directions.

articleTitle: A temporal continuity clustering algorithm for spatial-temporal data based on GMM and KNN
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: With the development of technology and the further exploration of space, the acquisition of numerous spatial-temporal data has become possible. How to use data mining technology, especially use clustering method, to analyze and derive information from spatial-temporal data to more effectively cope with real-world problems, has become an important issue. Based on the spatialtemporal temperature dataset covering 42 latitude and longitude points in one year, a new clustering algorithm combining GMM and KNN is developed to solve the problem of non-continuous time for within-cluster points. Then, this paper applies this clustering algorithm to the datasets of other time points in the same year and to the datasets of the subsequent year to explore the transferability of the algorithm and the availability of the classification results. The application results show that the proposed clustering algorithm can achieve temporal clustering of spatial-temporal data based on temperature while ensuring the temporal continuity of within-cluster points and the availability of classification results.

articleTitle: OAGAN: an oversampling approach for imbalanced data problems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Imbalanced data problems are prevalent in our daily lives. When conducted on this kind of data, many classification models may encounter many difficulties and produce ineffective performance due to a high training bias towards the majority of class instances. In order to solve the imbalanced data problem, many effective oversampling methods have been proposed. However, few methods in previous work consider different weights for minority class samples. Therefore, we proposed an oversampling method for the minority class by Adaptive Synthetic Sampling with Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (OAGAN) in this study. Firstly, Adaptive Synthetic Sampling is used to assign different weights to each minority class sample, based on which new similar samples are generated by the Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network. In other words, the weights of different minority class samples are considered when generating data using the Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network, thus improving the method. The proposed OAGAN method was evaluated on ten imbalanced datasets and three standard oversampling algorithms, which achieved better learning performance.

articleTitle: Comparative study on constitutive model of silicone rubber foam material
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The aging and degradation of mechanical properties in silicon foam materials are essential factors to be considered in the design of long-life and high-reliability structures. Through accelerated aging experiments on silicon foams and single-axis compression mechanical property tests on aged materials, the stress-strain relationship of silicon foams after different temperatures and aging times were obtained. Based on the commonly used hyperelastic constitutive model for compressible materials, a variable constitutive model was established based on the Arrhenius acceleration relationship and molecular aging kinetics equation. The correlation relationship between the constitutive model parameters and material aging time and temperature was regressed using the least squares method. The variable constitutive model was then established for silicon foam materials under single-axis compression. The experimental data was used as the basis for proposing the material variable constitutive model, which was tested through independent experiments and finite element analysis. The research results show that the variable constitutive model of silicon foams based on the Ogden Hyperfoam model can characterize the compression mechanical behaviour of silicon foams after different temperatures and aging times, providing a foundation for simulating the performance degradation of silicon foam structures and designing their life.

articleTitle: Transient dynamic finite element analysis and reliability assessment of mining excavators gear transmission system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: A transient dynamic finite element analysis and reliability assessment of mining excavators gear transmission system is conducted in this paper. Specifically, Transient dynamics method is used in mining excavator transmission gear contact finite element simulation analysis, studying the time-varying gear contact stress. Gear transmission three-dimension modeling was set up using UG software and imported into ANSYS for simulation analysis. According to the distribution of the motor power, and rotational speed, get the gear contact stress distribution, then depending on the materials of the gear tooth surface contact fatigue strength distribution, and get the gear contact fatigue reliability.

articleTitle: Optimal mission abort policy for partially observable three-state system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The survivability of safety-critical systems can be effectively improved by mission abort. Existing researches generally believe that the system state can be fully observed, but in fact, many systems cannot fully detect the health state during mission execution. For a typical three-state system, this paper studies a dynamic abort policy under the condition that the state information is partially observable, in which the state monitoring can only reveal part of the underlying state information. The issue is introduced and subsequently addressed using the framework of POMDP. The objective is to minimize the anticipated total cost resulting from both mission failure and system failure. Within this context, certain inherent characteristics of the value function and control limit strategy are elucidated and provided.

articleTitle: Scenario-based modeling and simulation of wartime equipment maintenance support process
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Aiming at the complex process of wartime equipment maintenance support and the changeable battle scenes, combined with the characteristics of wartime accompanying support and fixed-point support, based on vehicle routing problem and location problem, a modeling method of wartime equipment maintenance support process is proposed, a scenario-based model of wartime equipment maintenance support process is constructed, an improved firefly algorithm is designed to solve the model, and the effectiveness of the model and algorithm is verified by examples.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics analysis of a new precision roller gear transmission system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Using the concentrated mass approach, a two-degree-of-freedom dynamics model was developed to investigate the nonlinear dynamics of the new precision roller gear transmission system. During the meshing procedure, the model incorporates the torsional vibrations of the rollers and gears. Differential equations are derived using the Lagrange equation to describe the nonlinear dynamics of the transmission system, taking into account the linear stiffness of the contact pair and the mesh attenuation between meshing pairs. By adjusting the parameters of the brief amplitude factor K, mesh damping c, and roller diameter dr, the transmission system's nonlinear dynamics are solved using Matlab's Ode45 function. Diagrams such as the Lyaponuv exponential diagram, the bifurcation diagram, time domain diagram, phase plane diagram, Poincáre cross-section diagram, and spectrum diagram are utilized to examine nonlinear dynamics. According to our data, decreases in the brief amplitude coefficient K, the mesh damping coefficient c, and the roller diameter dr lead to a bifurcation into chaotic motion. As a result, the system's motion progresses from periodic to multiperiodic to chaotic. In the future, a novel precision roller gear transmission system could benefit from the findings of this study.

articleTitle: Optimization design of engine hood system for pedestrian protection and lightweight
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: With the increasingly strict pedestrian protection testing standards of C-IASI, the front end structure of automobiles also faces stricter design requirements. At the same time, the country has proposed a "dual carbon" strategy, and weight reduction of automobiles is also urgent. This article is based on the collision conditions between a 6-year-old child and a vehicle, constructing a finite element model for child collisions, and simplifying the finite element model, such as setting hard points and arranging hinges. In this paper, based on the topology optimization theory of variable density method, optimization and improvement are carried out. The final optimization form of the hood is obtained through optimization analysis. The weakening form of the inner plate is determined to be a longitudinal wide notch. At the same time, material replacement is carried out, and different mechanical performance analysis is carried out. Finally, aluminum alloy is selected as the material of the hood after comprehensive consideration of mechanical properties and quality. Finally, considering the three influencing factors affecting HIC, and then an enhanced NSGA -II Ualgorithm was proposed based on the enhanced NSGA-II U algorithm. Compared with NSGA-II, the enhanced algorithm combines structural optimization methods such as topology optimization and material optimization, and studies the coupling of attribute variables such as interior plate weakening scheme and numerical variables of structural parameters such as plate thickness. On this basis. The optimization goal is to reduce pedestrian head injury (HIC) and engine hood assembly quality, and ultimately achieve an 18% reduction in collision HIC compared to the initial engine hood.

articleTitle: Research on reliability simulation optimization design method for redundant systems considering component failure correlation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In response to the conventional approach of designing reliability for redundant systems, which often assumes independence among component failures and may not fully capture the true system reliability, this study introduces a novel reliability simulation design methodology that accounts for the correlation of component failures. Initially, a reliability design model for redundant systems, incorporating component failure correlation, is formulated using the copula function. Subsequently, an innovative simulation solution algorithm, grounded in the generalized reduced gradient method model, is developed. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed model and algorithm is demonstrated through a numerical illustration. The outcomes underscore the pronounced disparities in system reliability design strategies when considering the interdependency of component failures. This research furnishes valuable insights into optimizing the reliability design of equipment redundancy systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of RV reducers dynamic model parameters using a whale optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The dynamic model of rotary vector (RV) reducer is capable of simulating the actual running state of RV reducer and providing the simulation data of RV reducer running in various states. However, the dynamic model parameters of the RV reducer need to carefully selected to improve the precision of the corresponding dynamic responses, which is the focus of this work. Twentyfour dynamic model parameters, speed, torque, stiffnesses and dampings, are optimized using the whale optimization algorithm (WOA). Initial parameters and experimental data for an RV reducer are used as the starting point for the optimization. The optimized dynamics model parameters are determined, resulting in simulation data that exhibits a higher similarity with the experimental data than that using initial parameters.

articleTitle: Bayesian optimization-aided line sampling for estimating small failure probabilities
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Line sampling is recognized as an efficacious approach for addressing reliability analysis issues involving minute failure probabilities. Nonetheless, a central constraint of line sampling resides in the need for a dependable and precise principal direction, a task often arduous to accomplish for numerous intricate problems. To surmount this hurdle, this study exploits the full potential of our recently introduced Bayesian optimization technique designed for acquiring knowledge about the most probable points (MPPs). Within this framework, we introduce a novel algorithm termed Constrained Bayesian Subset Optimization (ConBaySubOpt) explicitly tailored for the active acquisition of MPPs within the context of reliability problems characterized by rare events. Subsequently, ConBaySubOpt serves as a preliminary search mechanism for identifying the pivotal direction in the subsequent line sampling procedure. Furthermore, the Gaussian process regression model established during the ConBaySubOpt process is harnessed as an initial step for actively estimating the intersection points of candidate line samples, referred to as intersection points (ISP). By this means, the injection of ConBaySubOpt can greatly enlarge the scope of line sampling method to treat nonlinear problem with rare event. The proposed method is illustrated by a ten-bar structure, the results show the superiority compared with other mostly advanced active learning approaches.

articleTitle: Human resource crisis warning for bearing manufacturing enterprises based on GRA and CV-AHP
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Enterprises are facing fierce competition and changes in the development of globalization and informatization, and human resources have become an important component of competitiveness. However, problems such as talent loss, job burnout, and employee dissatisfaction may lead to human resource crises in enterprises. This article takes bearing enterprises as an example to provide early warning for human resource crises. Firstly, a human resource crisis warning indicator system for bearing enterprises was constructed using GRA, and the indicator system was reduced; Secondly, an evaluation model was constructed using CV-AHP to reduce the impact of traditional AHP subjectivity; Finally, the feasibility of the method was verified through an example, providing reference and support for enterprise human resource crisis warning.

articleTitle: Reliability optimization of vertical axis wind turbine impeller
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The Vertical Axis Wind Turbine (VAWT) has attracted extensive research attention due to its inherent benefits, including straightforward manufacturing processes, low cost, and the elimination of the need for additional wind equipment. Currently, the majority of the existing research is concentrated on aerodynamics, while studies addressing the reliability of VAWTs are relatively scarce. In light of this, the present paper proposes a reliability optimization scheme for the VAWT impeller. Initially, the NSGA II optimization algorithm was employed for example verification, and a multi-objective optimization was conducted on the parameters of the VAWT impeller. The optimization objectives were identified as the minimization of the maximum equivalent stress and impeller mass, with the design variables being blade thickness and two-web thickness. The results demonstrate a reduction in the maximum equivalent stress by 25.57% and a decrease in mass by 6.88%. These findings substantiate the efficacy of the optimization and the reliability of the design scheme, contributing positively to the enhancement of VAWT reliability.

articleTitle: Defect detection technology of gas insulated switchgear based on ultra-high frequency method and ultrasonic method after earthquake
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Earthquake may cause defects in gas insulated switchgear (GIS) such as insulation cracks, foreign matters fall, high-voltage conductor looseness and even displacement, which brings serious threats to GIS safe operation. The above internal defects of GIS may trigger abnormal Ultra High Frequency (UHF) signals or ultrasonic signals. For that reason, this paper proposes the detecting and diagnosing method for the insulation internal discharge, floating potential discharge, free particles discharge of GIS after earthquake. By analyzing the characteristics such as frequency correlation, pulse amplitude dispersion, pulse time interval, pulse duration and pulse frequency domain distribution of different discharge type signals, GIS status evaluation and defect diagnosis can be achieved by combining the location of the defect. And it is helpful for improving the power grid's postearthquake recovery ability.

articleTitle: Fatigue spalling fault evolution analysis of an angular contact bearing of aeroengines
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Fatigue spalling of aeroengine bearings seriously affects the safety and stability of an aircraft. The existing technology of bearing fatigue spalling fault evolution analysis and life prediction is lacking. Once cracks occur, they need to be replaced and maintained, which wastes the life performance of the bearing to a certain extent. This paper conducted the fatigue spalling fault evolution analysis and life prediction of a 7208AC angular contact ball bearing's outer raceway. The finite element-based fatigue spalling fault evolution of the bearing is modeled, whose inputs contain the contacting parameters of the bearing calculated by a quasi-static model with the consideration of temperature and lubrication. The proposed method enables the analysis of the fatigue spalling fault evolution process in bearings. The analysis results are consistent with the general rule of bearing spalling. The proposed method can provide a new idea for the fatigue spalling fault evolution analysis and life prediction, and provide an important basis for aircraft emergency decision-making.

articleTitle: Improved prior distribution method for small sample maintainability verification
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In order to ascertain the accurate prior distribution of equipment maintainability parameters and secure the reliability of maintainability verification outcomes with small sample sizes, the study investigates the prior distribution determination techniques employing both the Bootstrap and Bayes Bootstrap methods. This research addresses a notable deficiency in the traditional Bootstrap method, wherein the new subsamples, generated based on its empirical distribution function, remain confined to the original sample data range and fail to converge to the actual distribution. An enhanced method for determining the prior distribution is proposed, featuring improvements in the resampling of regenerated samples and modification of the sample empirical distribution function using the "S" type Boltzmann sigmoid function. Simulation results indicate that this approach allows the new subsamples to transcend the constraints of the original data points' range, heightening the precision of maintainability parameter estimation, and securing a prior distribution more closely aligned with the genuine distribution. This lays a crucial groundwork for subsequent precise verification of equipment maintainability indicators.

articleTitle: Life distribution modeling for a buffered two-machine serial production system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The manufacturing industry is crucial to a country, and the operation and maintenance of machinery and equipment are also extremely important for production. As the impact of quality and reliability becomes increasingly prominent, maintenance during equipment degradation has received attention from researchers especially for the equipment degradation distribution based maintenance. For that reason, this paper focuses on this issue by collecting equipment failure time data from a certain enterprise, determining the data model, estimating its parameters, and finally conducting a test.

articleTitle: Research on IC chip reliability testing: the influence of ambient on IC junction temperature
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The junction temperature of a semiconductor IC chip is a key testing items for their reliability testing. However, there is currently no effective method available to quantitatively analyze the influence of environmental temperature on the junction temperature of an IC chip. This paper uses finite element analysis to analyze the effects of ambient temperatures such as heat conduction, convective heat transfer, radiation heat transfer and wind speed on the junction temperature of the IC chip. Thermal image is used to collect the junction temperature data of the IC chip at room temperature which serves as a criterion for evaluating the effectiveness of the model. Finally, an environmental model for the junction temperature of IC chips is established. This model enables accurate prediction of junction temperature variations under different environments, offering valuable theoretical support for the design and analysis of IC chip reliability.

articleTitle: State of health estimation for lithium batteries using improved weighted grey relational method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The State of Health (SOH) for lithium batteries is a crucial safety index, which is usually subjected to the many influencing factors including current, voltage, temperature, and so on. The existing direct indices to predict SOH have limitations with agreeable reliability. A new approach using multi-sensor fusion technology is proposed to construct a comprehensive health indicator for predicting SOH. Firstly, we calculate the probability density of each sensor for the charge/discharge cycle using the kernel probability density method. Secondly, we use the peak value of each probability density function as a new health index. Thirdly, we fuse the strongly correlated health indices using an improved grey correlation analysis method and use the comprehensive health indicator to estimate SOH. Thereafter, we conduct an experimental comparison study using publicly available degradation data of lithium batteries, and the results demonstrate that our method can effectively address the issues of incomplete consideration for influencing factors and low reliability of the SOH characterization indicators.

articleTitle: Research on fault propagation model of unmanned ground vehicle
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The escalating proliferation of unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) worldwide has underscored the critical importance of low-level reliability. This factor significantly constrains the widespread implementation of UGVs in battlefield scenarios. This paper addresses this pivotal issue by delving into the fault propagation model and its potential application to UGVs. The proposed methodology adopts a hierarchical directed graph model to depict the intricacies of fault propagation within UGVs. Specifically, this model serves as a framework for analyzing the fault propagation inherent in the conventional "Perception-Prediction-Planning-Control" process, which delineates the principal operational mechanism of UGVs. By amalgamating the model with empirical fault data gleaned from UGVs, it becomes viable to efficiently diagnose faults and discern anomalous phenomena.

articleTitle: EPF-Net: an anomaly detection model with an enhanced polarized self-attention
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: This paper focuses on building a high-performance defect detection model to detect unknown anomaly patterns in images without abnormal data. Defects in industrial parts being detected are an indispensable part of large-scale industrial manufacturing. At present, Machine vision-based defect detection technology has been widely employed in various industries, including 3C (Computer, Communication, and Consumer Electronics), textile, automotive, semiconductor, photovoltaic module, and other precision component products. This paper proposes an EPF-Net to better extract the pixel-level features with a different Polarization Self-Attention. Experiments are conducted on the MVTec AD dataset. The results demonstrate that our model is competitive with state-of-the-art anomaly detection models.

articleTitle: Investigating failure interaction in marine diesel power plants with FMECA
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: To determine the weaknesses of marine diesel power plant more accurately and reduce the risks brought by traditional failure mode analysis, qualitative analysis of main failure modes and failure cases of marine diesel power plant were carried out using failure mode effects analysis (FMEA) method in this paper. Subsequently, the House of Reliability (HoR) analysis method was embraced to refine the traditional criticality analysis (CA) approach, taking into account the interdependence of failures within the marine diesel power plant. This culminated in the derivation of hazards for each power plant subsystem, factoring in the implications of failure interactions. The FMECA analysis method in this paper overcomes defects of neglecting the influence of failure correlation and failure propagation, which can guide reliability design and evaluation analysis of marine diesel power plant.

articleTitle: Fault propagation analysis of complex electromechanical systems based on improved graph convolutional networks
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Aiming at a series of chain reactions such as propagation, diffusion, and CUSUM amplification caused by faults in complex electromechanical systems, the fault propagation mechanism of complex electromechanical systems is carried out. Based on the idea of node importance, the research improves the graph convolution network algorithm, integrates the structural indicators of the directed graph of fault propagation and the fault feature information of system component nodes, evaluates the system fault propagation behavior, and realizes the recognition of the fault propagation Critical path method of complex electromechanical systems. This method can compensate for the limitations of traditional fault propagation directed graph models that only consider structural indicators, achieve dynamic analysis of fault states, timely block fault propagation, reduce fault costs, and provide a theoretical basis for formulating effective fault prevention and control strategies.

articleTitle: Optimization design of power supply plug box heat dissipation based on Kriging surrogate of model
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The heat dissipation issue of the power supply plug box significantly affects its normal operation, making it a crucial factor to consider. Studies have shown that thermal failures account for about 55% of electronic equipment malfunctions[1]. Therefore, efficient heat dissipation design is paramount in product development. Hence, this article focuses on optimizing the heat dissipation design of a power supply plug box. Since the overall hardware layout has already been determined, the optimization process primarily revolves around improving the radiator's design. However, conventional optimization approaches involve costly continuous simulations and iterative experiments, hampering their practicality. To address this issue, the present study employs Kriging surrogate modeling to interpolate the power box insertion problem and establishes a corresponding mathematical model. Furthermore, an optimization framework based on the particle swarm optimization algorithm is constructed to minimize the design cost significantly. The obtained results demonstrate a modeling accuracy of 97.93% for the power supply plug box framework, indicating its high precision. Moreover, the optimized design successfully reduces the maximum temperature of the power supply box from 112.375 °C to 92.3427 °C, thereby effectively mitigating the risk of thermal failure.

articleTitle: A performance degradation prediction method based on GPR and physics of degradation for MEMS gyroscope
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical System) Gyroscopes can monitor the attitude of aircraft to achieve stable flight, which is one of the most critical part of automatic flight. Performance estimation and prediction with high accuracy for the MEMS gyroscope can improve the stability and reliability of quadrotor UAV. In practical application, the degradation of material property, operating environment, etc will affect the performance of gyroscope, physics of degradation analysis can help understand the performance degradation process more clearly. Therefore, in this paper, a performance degradation prediction method based on Gaussian process regression (GPR) and physics of degradation modelling is developed. The mail performance indicators and degradation mechanism of MEMS gyroscopes are analysed, on this basis, the performance degradation process is simulated by Simulink. The prediction results based on one-dimension degradation data, two-dimension degradation data and three-dimension degradation data are compared, which proves that three-dimension degradation data can predict the remaining life of the MEMS gyroscope with high precision.

articleTitle: Reliability modeling and maintenance decision for a k-out-of-n: F system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Redundancy is commonly designed as a critical unit in complex engineering systems to improve their reliability. Among the redundant structures, the k-out-of-n structure is the most useful. In this paper, reliability modeling and maintenance decisionmaking are investigated for a k-out-of-n: F subsystem. Firstly, the Weibull distribution is used to describe the component degradation process, and the influence of external damage shock on the component degradation process is considered. Secondly, the component-level reliability model and the system-level reliability model of the system are established. The failures are classified as Class I failures and Class II failures. The system is repaired by minimum repair, component replacement, and preventive maintenance, respectively. Finally, the optimal maintenance strategy was derived by minimizing the expected cost per unit.

articleTitle: Research on modeling and clustering algorithm of unmanned aerial vehicle swarm network under search task
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Analogous to smart swarm, UAV swarms are developing towards decentralization and self-organization. The basic functional requirements such as networking and information interaction during mission execution are constrained by airborne energy, and clustering algorithm is an effective way to improve mission efficiency. Therefore, it is meaningful to establish a drone cluster motion model for specific tasks and conduct experiments on clustering algorithms in the model. In order to achieve the above goals, this paper firstly models the swarm based on the complex network theory, and then divides the task grids in the limited search area. Based on the task grids and the attractiveness of neighbour nodes, the classic Vicsek model is improved by considering the location awareness, regional interaction. Based on the simplified task of area search, a method combines individual movement module, information module and energy module with task scene module is proposed. Then an improved weighted clustering method that comprehensively considers individual energy remaining, neighbour node degree difference, maximum similarity speed and centrality is proposed, and combined with search task scenario. Several classic algorithms of clustering management in the process of collaborative task are evaluated and compared with the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Remaining useful life prediction of spherical plain bearing based on incremental Kalman filter
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: There is an implicit assumption that two adjacent moments have the same state quantity in the traditional Kalman filter-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction method, which may result in a low prediction accuracy. To overcome this issue, a novel RUL prediction method of spherical plain bearing is proposed based on an incremental Kalman filter (IKF). Firstly, a degradation model is constructed based on Wiener process for spherical plain bearing. Then, the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method is used to get the initial parameters. Furthermore, the RUL of spherical plain bearing is predicted based on IKF. Finally, an engineering example involving spherical plain bearing is used to verify the proposed method. The results show that the prediction accuracy of the proposed method can be effectively improved compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Time-dependent reliability analysis of flapping-wing mechanism considering truncated random variables
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Time-dependent reliability evaluation is an advantageous approach to estimate the failure probability of a mechanism in its motion period. Truncated random variables exist in most mechanisms, and considering this factor can extra precisely consider the time-dependent reliability of mechanisms. This article proposes an established approach for time-dependent reliability evaluation of mechanisms thinking about truncated random variables. Firstly, the motion error function is established, and the input parameters are transformed from truncated variables to truncated standard normal variables. Then, the envelope function approach for remodeling time-dependent reliability troubles into time-independent reliability troubles hassle at a couple of time enlargement points. On this basis, the saddle point approximation method is used to calculate the failure likelihood at the expansion point, and the Gaussian-copula function is used to calculate the joint failure probability. Finally, the higher and decrease bounds of the complete failure chance are obtained through the second-order narrow reliability bounds. The application results on the flapping-wing mechanism show that the method can accurately and efficiently evaluate the time-dependent reliability of the mechanism thinking about the truncated random variables.

articleTitle: A method for military entity relation extraction based on two-level attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: To address the challenge of limited training data for entity relation extraction in the military domain, training instances within this domain are automatically generated employing the distant supervision method. Subsequently, to mitigate the problem of noise in corpus construction, a two-level attention model for entity relation extraction (RE) is introduced. Following the bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BI-GRU) network, instance-level and word-level attention mechanisms are incorporated. This allows the model to initially capture bidirectional semantic information of the training instances through BI-GRU. Subsequently, it employs word-level attention to identify crucial words within each training instance, and introduces instance-level attention across multiple training instances, emphasizing the key examples. Experiments conducted on the automatically constructed training corpus in the military domain illustrate the model's effective entity relation extraction capabilities. Furthermore, it mitigates the influence of noise data introduced through distant supervision, thereby enhancing the accuracy of relation extraction.

articleTitle: Microalgae collaborate with microorganisms to purify the aquaculture waste water
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-level indoor wastewater treatment mode of `microalgae-microorganisms' for industrial marine aquaculture was established, a water purification facility for microalgae was designed, and the content of pollutants in water was explored by microalgae and microorganisms.
