The results showed that the `microalgae + microorganism' wastewater treatment system treated ammonia nitrogen (NH4+-N), nitrate nitrogen (NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>-N), nitroso nitrogen (NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>-N), inorganic nitrogen (TIN), inorganic phosphorus (PO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-</sup>-P), and chemical oxygen demand (COD) in wastewater. The maximum removal rates are 100%, 87%, 100%, 89%, 85% and 71%, respectively. Microalgae synergistic microbial water purification is conducive to the removal of nutrient rich substances in water, and provides a reference for ecological water purification and resource utilization of industrial agriculture wastewater.

articleTitle: Fatigue life prediction method of nuclear pipelines based on convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Deep learning models have powerful feature extraction and nonlinear fitting capabilities, which make deep learning show superior results in various industries. How to combine deep learning related theories with traditional fatigue life prediction methods to predict the fatigue life of nuclear pipelines more accurately is a direction worth exploring. This paper proposes a fatigue life prediction method for nuclear pipelines, which can make full use of the original data and features to predict the fatigue life. Firstly, the fatigue life of the corresponding samples is calculated based on the vibration signal of the nuclear pipeline using the rain flow counting method. Secondly, the time domain, frequency domain, and time-frequency domain features of the vibration signal are calculated, and the fatigue life and sample features are composed of a sample set. Then, the random forest algorithm is used to calculate the feature importance of each sample in the sample set, obtain sensitive features, and form a new sample set for training and verification of the convolutional neural network. Based on the results, it is evident that the method shows an improved ability to predict the fatigue life of the nuclear pipeline.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of riveting process of composite materials
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: According to the connection characteristics of composite multi-riveted structure, parametric design language APDL was used to conduct finite element modeling in ANSYS classical interface. Considering the random characteristics of the material, size, load and other parameters of the research object, taking the row distance of the rivet, the distance between the rivet and the edge of the thin plate, the distance between the rivet and the front end of the thin plate were taken as the influencing parameters, the variation trend of the maximum displacement of the riveted joint structure under different working conditions was analyzed. The reliability sensitivity values of the relevant random parameters were calculated by the Latin hypercube sampling method, and the random parameters which have great influence on the reliability of the riveted structure were obtained, which can be applied to more complex riveted joint structures.

articleTitle: Reliability modeling of mechanical structures considering strength degradation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: A new method for calculating structural reliability under impact load conditions based on the energy method is proposed. Using this method, the energy magnitude of the impact load acting on the structure is first analyzed using the Parseval's theorem, and the time-domain expression of the impact load signal is given. On the basis of energy conservation, the stress expression generated by the impact load on the structure is calculated, derive a structural reliability model under impact load conditions based on the stress intensity interference model. The failure forms of structural strength are analyzed, including degradation failure and degradation failure process with impact, and describe the degradation process of strength through Wiener process. Establish a structural reliability analysis model under impact load under the premise of strength degradation. Verify the accuracy and practicality of the model through example analysis, and the results show that the model can accurately describe the degradation process of strength, The effective calculation of structural reliability has certain guiding significance for the reliability analysis of mechanical structures under impact loads.

articleTitle: Maintenance decision of repairable series system with k-out-of-n: F subsystems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Series production systems are widely applied in production, and safety-critical components that play a key role in production are particularly important. The redundant design of safety-critical components can not only improve the reliability of the system but also save maintenance costs. Due to this fact, this paper proposed a maintenance strategy for the series production system by focusing on two objectives: maximization of system reliability and minimization of system maintenance cost. The system in view consists of k-out-of-n: F subsystems as well as single component subsystems that are connected in series. In redundant subsystems, the components are assumed to be independent and identical. By implementing this maintenance strategy, the goal is to improve the overall reliability of the system while minimizing the cost associated with maintenance activities. To analyze their performances, an iterative algorithm is used in numerical examples, and the result shows that the maintenance policy proposed is effective and practical.

articleTitle: Analysis on the relationship between R&D cost control and design reliability in scientific and technological enterprises
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The product R&D funds invested by scientific and technological innovation enterprises in the design and development process account for a large proportion of the entire enterprise's operating costs. If reliability design verification and process control are not done well in product design and manufacturing, various quality problems will occur after the product puts on the market. The resulting return and maintenance bring huge after-sales operation costs to enterprises. From the perspective of R&D cost control, this paper discusses the relationship between cost control, profit improvement and the introduction of product reliability design verification. It can provide useful thinking for enterprises to reduce design and development costs and after-sales operation costs.

articleTitle: Reliability assessment of machine tool spindle systems with fault-free data
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of evaluating the reliability of the spindle subsystem in the TK6913 heavy-duty CNC boring and milling machine, especially in the absence of fault data, a novel approach is proposed. By focusing on the spindle cooling subsystem, the concept of approximation is introduced. Similar machine tools' spindle cooling subsystem fault data post virtual expansion is adopted as the primary basis for reliability assessment. Moreover, the fault data from the spindle cooling subsystem, enriched through subjective expert insights, is incorporated as supplementary input for refining the evaluation outcomes. Ultimately, the parameter estimation results derived from the two data sets following expansion are combined through weighting and fusion. This culminates in the attainment of reliability assessment outcomes for the spindle cooling subsystem via the weighted fusion approach. The modeling, evaluation methods, and evaluation results used in this paper can provide a reference and theoretical basis for the reliability study of heavy-duty CNC machine tools when there is no trouble-free data.

articleTitle: Geometrically exact shell element with director undergoing finite rotation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: This paper introduces novel quadrilateral shell elements, which adhere to the concept of "geometrically exact" formulation and account for finite rotations. Within the framework of the Cosserat director theory, the shell's complexity is reduced by treating it as a mid-surface featuring outward directors. The study outlines two distinct approaches to describe the rotations of the directors. The first approach defines a pseudo-rotation vector characterized by only two components, while the second employs two independent spherical coordinates to define the director's orientation. By incorporating the Assumed Natural Strain (ANS) method, the paper presents second-order quadrilateral shell elements that consist of nine nodes and effectively eliminate shearlocking issues. These elements exhibit a streamlined representation of the director's motion, utilizing a minimal set of five components per node. The efficacy of the proposed shell elements is demonstrated through two numerical simulations aimed at validation. Furthermore, a comparative analysis between the predictions of these newly developed shell elements and those generated by commercial codes is conducted.

articleTitle: Adaptability test research of aerospace products under shock environment
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In this paper, a test verification method of aerospace products under shock environment is studied. According to the study, using the shock response spectrum of the mounting surface as a test verification method for the shock environment adaptability of a single machine can easily cause inaccurate test results and make it difficult to accurately assess the shock environment adaptability for target products. Under the condition that the existing standards and methods remain unchanged, it is recommended that using the shock response spectrum from the base of the single machine installation point as the test object would yield more scientifically sound and precise evaluations of the single machine's shock environment adaptability.

articleTitle: A method for bearing health condition assessment based on A-R TCN observer
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The health status of bearings is of great importance to the reliability of rotating machinery and equipment. In this paper, the observer-based method is used to construct residuals from bearing vibration data, and aims to establish a health benchmark by extracting a sequence of residual features from the bearing during normal operation. Furthermore, it measures the similarity between the residual features obtained from the bearing during full-life operation and the former, thereby inferring the health condition of the bearing during operation. Given the good performance of temporal convolutional networks in sequence prediction and the role of the self-attentive mechanism in connecting various parts of the input, the attention-residual temporal convolutional network (A-R TCN) is proposed in this paper, which combines the two and uses residual connections as an observer. Given the correlation between features, scale and sample distribution, the similarity measure of the residual features is measured using the Mahalanobis distance. Experiments show that the A-R TCN observer has better overall performance than the GRNN, LSTM and TCN observers in terms of mean square error, mean absolute error and forward inference speed, and the health condition curves have good discrimination between the health of the bearings at each moment.

articleTitle: Failure propagation analysis study of industrial robot based on meta-action
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The structures of industrial robots are complex, and they consist of numerous parts. The fault analysis of current industrial robots usually targets a single component or a part, ignoring the fault propagation relationship of the parts. Due to the large number of parts and complex coupling, it is difficult to find the key unit that affects the whole machine, thus this paper proposes a fault propagation analysis method based on meta-action. Firstly, the whole machine is decomposed using the Function-Motion-Action (FMA) decomposition method to obtain each meta-action unit. Secondly, the fault data are combined with the expert experience after fuzzification to jointly construct the initial relationship matrix of the meta-action units and draw the corresponding fault propagation directed graph. Thirdly, the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) and the Interpretive Structural Model (ISM) are used to stratify the fault propagation directed graph, to rank the importance of meta-action units to get the key meta-action units, and to carry out the impact analysis between meta-action unit faults. The analysis of a certain model of robot R500 as an example verifies the practicality of the method in this paper.

articleTitle: A gallbladder cancer classification model based on global-local NET
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Medical imaging data-based computer-aided diagnosis technology is being employed more and more frequently due to the quick advancement of artificial intelligence technology. The most frequent malignant tumor in the biliary tract, gallbladder cancer has a high degree of aggressiveness and a bad prognosis. As a benign chronic gallbladder inflammation, xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis is non-specific in clinical manifestation compared with gallbladder cancer. Preoperative correct identification of gallbladder cancer and xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis is of great importance for doctors to choose surgical methods. Therefore, this paper intends to establish a classification model for gallbladder cancer and xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis through deep learning methods to provide clinical decision support for doctors. This paper analyzes the performance of convolutional neural network and Transformer algorithms in terms of global feature and local feature extraction, and proposes Global-Local Net. Using CT images as datasets, classification models for gallbladder cancer and xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis were constructed based on EfficientNet, Vision Transformer and Global-Local Net, respectively. According to the testing findings, the accuracy of the Global-Local Net can reach 0.9000 and 0.943, and the AUC can reach 0.848 and 0.895 on the arterial phase CT dataset and venous phase CT dataset, respectively.

articleTitle: Study of the method of determining a pass-fail sequential sampling test scheme
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: This article studies the method of determining the sampling test plan of pass-fail products. The warhead, engine, battery, and torpedo equipment are all typical pass-fail products. Studying the sequential sampling test scheme of such products is the groundwork for carrying out reliability acceptance and evaluation tests. In the past, reliability verification tests for pass-fail products were mainly conducted by purposefully selecting appropriate test schemes from national standards. Due to the particularity of the plans listed in the standards, they were unable to meet all situations, and even the reliability level results obtained from the tests could not reflect the actual situation. In order to calculate and analyze specific experiments and their constraints, and complete the design of test schemes, this paper proposes a sequential sampling test scheme design method for pass-fail products. The effectiveness of the method has been verified through theoretical analysis and simulation calculations.

articleTitle: Driver abnormal behavior detection system using two-stage object detection
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Detection of abnormal driving behavior by drivers is a serious issue, as it will lead to accidents and increase traffic burden. To reduce the number of traffic accidents caused by abnormal driver behaviors, a safety assistance system has been developed. The system contains a two-stage object detection approach that is capable of detecting abnormal driving behavior in real-time. The lightweight face detection network used in the first stage can capture facial and head pose information about the driver and perform dynamic cropping of the captured image to obtain a smaller size. This operation will result in a reduction in parameter count and improved accuracy of the behavior model in the second stage. The experiments conducted showed that this method increased detection speed by 3 to 4 times while improving model accuracy. Moreover, the cropped area can perform various tasks inside the cabin, extending its usefulness with the collaboration of the ADAS.

articleTitle: A study of prognostics and health management standardization
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) is a maintenance assurance method to ensure the equipment reliability and safety and achieve scientific management of information and maintenance resources by sensing equipment status information, assessing health status and predicting remaining life, and taking timely measures before failure occurs. In view of the real requirement for engineering application of PHM technology, we focus on the related contents of PHM standard research and its required analysis at home and abroad. The PHM standard system of major foreign standardization organizations is tracked and studied, and the existing standards are systematically sorted out. The problems and development directions are analyzed so as to lay the foundation for the study of PHM standard system in China. Based on the study of PHM-related concepts, theories and methods, the requirement for PHM technology application in China is analyzed. Further, the necessity and feasibility of PHM standardization research are discussed and the rationalized suggestions are eventually put forward.

articleTitle: Life simulation analysis of wind turbine blade coating in the random wind and rain field
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The use of a protective coating to enhance the weatherability of blades has become a reliable, economical, and important means to ensure aerodynamic performance and prolong the life of blades. In this paper, the model of the 3MW horizontal axis wind turbine blade was established by the Glauert method, and then the 3D model of a 2mm PU coating was established. According to the measured data, the parameters of the Weibull distribution model of wind speed are obtained, and the particle size distribution and final velocity of raindrops are calculated using Bester's empirical formula. The coupling field of blade coating was established in Workbench, and the damage and life of blade coating were analyzed with ANSYS software. Simulation analysis shows that the maximum instantaneous stress response of the coating is 2.79 MPa, which is located far from the blade rotation center and close to the blade tip. This area is close to the maximum cumulative damage area of the coating, and the fatigue life of the coating is about 6.3 years. The research results have guiding value for the design and maintenance of wind turbine blade coatings.

articleTitle: Sensor monitoring driven identification of heterogeneous working conditions for machine tool
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: With the development of intelligent manufacturing, real-time and adaptive RUL prediction will become a strong demand for intelligent processing centers. The heterogeneity of working conditions makes the lifetime present highly nonlinear, increasing the uncertainty of RUL prediction. Despite the development of various adaptive RUL prediction methods, the identification technique of heterogeneous working conditions is still a gap. To realize an adaptive or real-time RUL prediction, the identification of current working conditions and state transition trajectories of future working conditions is necessary. Therefore, by utilizing various monitored sensor data, a similarity evaluation method for working-condition identification is proposed. First, two features, the deviation between the probability density functions (PDF) in the amplitude domain and the crosscorrelation coefficient in the time domain are constructed. Then, a similarity evaluation method is proposed by constructing the similarity level of two sensor data samples, where two different evaluating indexes are provided for the similarity level. One is evaluated by the average difference of sample features from different sensors under two different working conditions, and another is by the Euclidean distance of sample features under two different working conditions. Then, a comparison method based on 24 time-domain and frequency-domain features is given to verify the performance of the proposed method. At last, a case study based on a degradation dataset of milling insert is provided, proving the effectiveness of our proposed method. Also, the impact of different data manipulations on the accuracy rate of identifications is discussed in the case study

articleTitle: Research on reliability allocation problem based on improved particle swarm optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: To achieve the optimal reliability allocation scheme that meets the system reliability requirements while minimizing the cost, an improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed in this paper. The optimal allocation scheme is iteratively solved by taking the lowest total allocation cost as the objective function and taking into account the upper and lower limit constraints of component reliability and system reliability index constraints. This paper adopts the four parameter cost reliability model commonly used in engineering to establish an objective function. For the upper and lower limit constraints of component reliability, a correction link is added to the classical PSO algorithm to ensure that the particles generated in each iteration meet the component reliability constraints. For system reliability index constraints, a discard link is added to the classical PSO algorithm to ensure that each particle is a feasible solution. Finally, the above improved PSO algorithm is realized through a numerical example. And compared with other algorithms in the literature, it shows that the improved PSO algorithm can simultaneously obtain the optimization results of the lowest total allocation cost and the highest system reliability.

articleTitle: Effects of different gas conditions on quality of live Patinopecten yessoensis in sealed packaging transportation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)

The results showed that the survival rate of scallops packed with aerated ratio 80%O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>20%N2 and 100%O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was higher. The total number of colonies was at least 4.8× 103CFU/g. The glycogen content decreased the slowest. The texture quality remained higher and the survival effect was better. articleTitle: Surrogate modeling of engine performance parameters using regularizing generative adversarial networks
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: We propose a new surrogate modeling method based on regularizing generative adversarial models. The method first performs design of experiments (DoE) and numerical experiments on the surrogate object to obtain a basic engine performance dataset. The generated data is used to train an improved regularized generative adversarial network to build a surrogate model of engine performance parameters, solving the difficult problem of high cost and poor security in obtaining reliable data in industry. To address the problem that observed data can be corrupted by complex noise in real industrial environments, we add noise to the high-fidelity dataset and verify the feasibility and robustness of the method. Based on the experimental results, our method produces a surrogate model that is able to return predictive outputs that take noise into account. Our method demonstrates superior accuracy compared to other classical surrogate algorithms, successfully capturing the essential characteristics of surrogate objects.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of DC motor-reducer system using a H∞ unknown input observer
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In this study, a fault diagnosis approach is introduced, employing a H∞ unknown input observer (UIO) to address the intricate issue that fully decoupling the unknown input in the DC motor-reducer system is challenging. Firstly, a state-space model is established for the DC motor-reducer system. Secondly, the equation condition of the Unknown Input Observer (UIO) is used to decompose the unknown input into decoupled and uncoupled parts. The decouplable part is then eliminated from the estimation error, and a residual generator for the UIO is designed using the H∞ performance index to ensure robustness against the uncoupled part. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed H∞ UIO is validated through simulation. The simulation outcomes demonstrate the method's efficacy in diagnosing additive and multiplicative sensor faults within the DC motor-reducer system.

articleTitle: A new curved surface integral method for reliability analysis
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The numerical analytical methods (such as the Second-Order Reliability Method and the First-Order Reliability Method) are efficient approaches. However, they may still result in significant errors in some nonlinear problems. Simulation methods (such as Monte Carlo Method and Subset Simulation method) have good accuracy but lack efficiency. The approximate model method (such as Kriging, Artificial Neural Networks and the Support Vector Machines) can be used to solve the black box problem, but it still needs to be combined with analytical or simulation methods, so the drawbacks of numerical analytical methods and simulation methods still exist. This paper proposes a new Curved Surface Integral (CSI) approach for reliability analysis, it is based on the intersection of reliability index β-circles and the parabolic constraint. The CSI approach computes the failure probability by integrating over the intersection area. In addition, this paper briefly introduces the radial hyperspace partitioning approach and the hyper-sphere segmentation numerical integration method for reliability analysis. Finally, the robustness and feasibility of CSI are proved by two examples, and the results show that the proposed CSI approach is effective.

articleTitle: Optimization of non-normal distribution for product tolerance considering asymmetric cubic quality loss
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In the realm of product quality, the distribution of errors can exhibit variability and may not consistently adhere to a normal distribution. On occasions, the quality attributes of a product might exhibit deviations from normality. Consequently, the investigation delves into the utilization of the asymmetric cubic quality loss and the trapezoidal distribution, a frequently employed non-normal distribution. Given the inherent asymmetry in quality loss, optimizing the process mean becomes instrumental in diminishing anticipated quality loss. Within the framework of the trapezoidal distribution, we propose an expected loss model that takes into account varying distances between the process mean and the target value, facilitating the optimization of the process mean. The uncertainty associated with measurements leads to measurement loss, a concern mitigated through integration with the quality loss function. Ultimately, building upon the proposed model, a tolerance model is formulated, serving as the objective function for determining the optimal tolerance. The viability of the model is showcased through a provided illustrative example.

articleTitle: Research on the reliability of wire bonding in humid environments
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In order to study the reliability of bonding wire under the condition of humidity environment, a testing structure chip was designed and three samples were subjected to humid test at 85°C/85% RH. During the experiment, all three samples showed an increase in leakage current. Through on-site observations, it was found that the leakage current occurred initially, when the experiment continued, the test structure failed due to the detachment of bonding wires from the bonding pad. The failure analysis showed that the surface of the passivation layer between adjacent aluminium pads was covered with impurities, including carbon (C), sodium (Na), aluminium (Al), tungsten (W), and chlorine (Cl) elements. The presence of these conductive elements resulted in leakage between two adjacent aluminium pads on the chip surface that had different electronic potentials. The detachment of bonding wires from the bonding pad is attributed to a chemical reaction caused by vapors. This reaction corrodes the metal aluminium on the bonding pad, leading to the formation of aluminium oxide, causing the gold wire to detach from the pad, and the lifetime of the bonding wire solder joints has been calculated.

articleTitle: Service life assessment method for large excavator based on evidence fusion
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The data deficiency is a universal phenomenon in excavator service life evaluation with classical probabilistic method. In order to solve the problem of small sample in excavator life evaluation, all kinds of storage information in the development process is fully utilized. In this paper, the evidence theory is used to integrate the main and objective information such as field test, laboratory test and expert comprehensive evaluation of each engine component. Therefore, the identification framework of excavator life and the basic probability assignment (BPA) calculation method based on the evidence network (EN) model are established. This method is used to evaluate the life of an excavator. The results show that the method is accurate and the estimated life of the excavator reaches the first maintenance cycle. The proposed method can make full use of all kinds of service life data in development, and is expected to provide a new technical approach for excavator service life evaluation with insufficient information.

articleTitle: RUL prediction of rolling bearings based on ISSA-CNN-BiGRU
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: To address the challenges of low prediction accuracy and poor generalization ability in the remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of bearings, a novel prediction method based on an improved variational sparrow search algorithm (ISSA) and CNNBiGRU is proposed. The hyperparameters of the CNN-BiGRU are automatically optimized by the ISSA with dynamic searchability. The trained ISSA-CNN-BiGRU model is used for the bearing RUL prediction. The generalization ability and performance of the proposed method are verified in different datasets. The ISSA-CNN-BiGRU model outperforms the other benchmark methods in bearing RUL prediction, which demonstrates the better performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Introducing feature matching and smoothing loss: a novel GAN for improved sample generation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Fault diagnosis of planetary gearboxes constitutes a vital element of rotating machinery. In recent years, fault diagnosis techniques for planetary gearboxes predicated on deep learning have undergone extensive research. However, in scenarios with limited samples, these deep learning methodologies can grapple with data scarcity issues, negatively impacting the model's generalization capacity and diagnostic performance. To mitigate this, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been integrated into planetary gearbox fault diagnosis to fabricate synthetic data, thereby augmenting the training dataset. Nevertheless, GANs face challenges in effectively learning local feature information from samples, leading to substantial disparities in local features between the generated data and the original data. Furthermore, the sampling of fault vibration signals from planetary gearboxes often exhibits a high frequency, with relatively smooth signal transitions, while the vibration signal samples generated by GANs often fluctuate excessively, demonstrating significant differences from the original vibration signals. To address this issue, this study introduces an enhanced GAN network that incorporates a feature attention matching mechanism in the computation of the loss function. This mechanism aims to amplify the feature similarity between the generated samples and local samples. Concurrently, a smoothness loss is introduced into the loss function to ensure the changes in the generated signal samples are more gradual. Experimental results indicate that this proposed method can generate superior quality samples, and the generated samples can achieve high accuracy on the WD-CNN diagnostic network.

articleTitle: Reliability-based design optimization based on weighted simulation and Kriging model
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Many existing methodologies for reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) necessitate the exploration of the most probable point (MPP), posing challenges in offering optimal solutions for intricate issues. In Ref.[13], an efficacious RBDO approach grounded in weighted simulation was introduced as a remedy to this quandary. This method exhibits robustness and obviates the need for MPP search. Nonetheless, when encountering implicit constraints entailing time-intensive simulations, it could potentially incur substantial computational costs. To surmount this hurdle, an extension is proposed through the integration of adaptive Kriging models, thereby replacing resource-intensive implicit functions with Kriging models to alleviate the computational load. The viability and effectiveness of the presented technique are confirmed through an empirical examination involving a reliability test problem.

articleTitle: Risk assessment of complex product supply chain from the perspective of big data
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The global situation has become volatile in recent years, marked by frequent regional conflicts and significant crises impacting the global supply chain. This paper utilizes big data analysis technology to identify, analyze, and evaluate the risks associated with complex product supply chains. The primary types of supply chain risks are categorized as supplier risk and product risk. Leveraging big data technology, various risk factors are analyzed, and the paper presents risk assessment methods and implementation steps. This study aims to provide a fresh perspective on risk management in complex product supply chains.

articleTitle: MTBF evaluation of key components of wind turbine based on multi-source data
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of inadequate observation data for the reliability assessment of newly deployed wind turbines. It introduces a methodology for evaluating the reliability of key wind turbine components, grounded in multi-source data. By constructing a fusion algorithm of fault data and performance degradation data, using Monte Carlo sampling technology to realize unit fault data expansion and fusion. Based on the fusion data, distribution function primary, goodness of fit test, parameter estimation, and reliability estimation are carried out. Finally, the reliability of key components of the unit, MTBF, and reliable life of the point estimation and interval estimation. The effectiveness of the method is verified by taking a gearbox as an example.

articleTitle: A data-driven framework of predicting the effective switching cycles of on-load tap-changer considering degradation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The total number of switching cycles is the most crucial performance index of the on-load tap-changer (OLTC), which determines its lifespan. Thus, this study explores a method to estimate the effective switching cycle number of OLTC based on the Kriging model considering degradation. First, the mechanical fault causes of the OLTC are analysed via establishing the fault tree, by which the principal factors of spring stress relaxation and parts wear that affect the switching cycle are determined. Then, the parameters with respect to the factors over the whole performance life are accurately identified and matched with the help of testing data. Subsequently, based on the transition time, the precise dynamic model of OLTC is constructed, and the contact separation time under the deterministic condition is obtained and verified using dynamic analysis strategy. Finally, the sampling data and corresponding contact separation time are introduced into the Kriging model, and then the effective switching cycle number is predicted according to the failure criterion. This study can provide a new data-driven framework for lifespan prediction of OLTC.

articleTitle: Reliability-based topology optimization using the sequential optimization and reliability assessment
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In order to comprehensively address uncertainties inherent in structural design and topology optimization, we introduce a novel approach known as reliability-based topology optimization (RBTO). This paper's principal contribution lies in leveraging the sequential optimization and reliability assessment (SORA) strategy to disentangle the original nested RBTO procedure into discrete topology optimization (TO) and reliability analysis (RA) processes. This separation facilitates an alternating sequence of TO and RA within the optimization framework. During the TO phase, we employ the solid isotropic material with penalization (SIMP) method and the bi-directional evolutionary structural optimization (BESO) method to construct distinct TO models. Meanwhile, the RA step adopts a performance measure approach (PMA) augmented by a Kriging model, thereby reducing the computational burden associated with calculating sensitivity of the constraint function concerning random variables in the RA process. Ultimately, we present two illustrative examples involving a cantilever beam and an L-shaped beam design, each characterized by varying objective and constraint functions. These case studies serve to underscore the practical applicability and soundness of our proposed RBTO methodology.

articleTitle: Environmental adaptability analysis and performance degradation characterization parameters study of fluorosilicone rubber ring for ultra high voltage GIS equipment
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: With the widespread application of ultra-high voltage GIS equipment in various regions of the country, the climate environment in different regions also poses great challenges to the selection of rubber materials for sealing. Under different climatic and environmental conditions, the failure modes and performance degradation rates of rubber materials are also different. To meet the high-reliability requirements of ultra-high voltage GIS equipment, it is urgent to conduct environmental adaptability and performance degradation analysis of rubber materials, to provide a basis for material selection. This article takes fluorosilicone rubber used in ultra-high voltage GIS equipment as the object, analyzes its typical application scenarios and main failure modes, and determines its performance characterization parameter set, failure influencing factors, and value range based on the analysis of its failure mechanism. Based on this, environmental adaptability tests and aging life tests under simulated working conditions were designed, and the environmental adaptability analysis of the fluoroether rubber seal was completed based on the test data. According to the principle of correlation and monotonicity, the optimal performance characterization parameters of the fluorosilicone rubber material are determined by comparing the change rule of each parameter in the performance characterization parameter set with the aging time, providing support for the design, selection, use, and maintenance of the fluorosilicone rubber material for the subsequent ultra-high pressure GIS equipment.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of intelligent cleaning robots based on FMECA and FTA
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Driven by scientific and technological advancements and societal progress, there is a growing demand for intelligent cleaning robots. These robots find extensive application in domains characterized by perilous conditions, intricate tasks, substantial labor expenses, and suboptimal efficiency. An intelligent cleaning robot operates as a mechatronics system, guided by preprogrammed motion patterns. Given the impact of numerous uncertain variables on work quality during the operation of cleaning robots, investigating the reliability of these robots assumes paramount significance as a key avenue of development. This paper analyzes the reliability of intelligent cleaning robots through FMECA and FTA. The cleaning robot is divided into subsystems and failure modes. Severity analysis and improvement measures are put forward. The importance of the cleaning robot is judged by ranking the harm degree of the sub-systems. The minimum cut set of the system fault is given by establishing the fault tree of the cleaning robot for qualitative analysis, and the probability of subsystem fault is calculated by quantitative analysis, which can improve the reliability of the robot system.

articleTitle: Faults identification with deep CNN fine-tuned ResNet50 model for rolling bearings
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: There is broad use of rotating machinery in various industrial practices. The diagnosis of rolling bearing defects in rotating machinery is a broad area in all engineering disciplines since these errors might result in production losses and downtime. Machine learning approaches have been successfully used in recent years to diagnose these faults, with transfer learning being a promising approach that can be used with limited data. Transfer learning refers to the technique of leveraging knowledge gained from one domain to improve prediction and learning in another. The proposed approach in this paper uses a pre-trained ResNet50-TL deep neural network to extract features from 2D RGB scalogram images, which were created from 1D vibration signals by using the continuous wavelet transform technique. These 2D scalogram images were then used to train a ResNet50- TL classifier model for fault classification and identification. The proposed method was tested on a real-world public dataset of rolling bearings created by Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), outperforming other cutting-edge methods in terms of accuracy. An accurate fault identification method using transfer learning with the proposed method has been shown to be highly effective, demonstrating its applications in rotating machinery and achieving 99.6% test accuracy.

articleTitle: Structure design and gait transition stability of quadruped robot
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In a manner akin to mammals, quadruped robots must select specific gaits corresponding to the terrain in order to curtail energy consumption and enhance ambulatory efficiency. Gait transition, constituting a pivotal facet of quadrupedal robot locomotion research, profoundly embodies the robot's motion prowess. Effectuating real-time gait adjustments while ensuring seamless transition stands as a formidable undertaking, encompassing the investigation into gait transition stability. Presently, within the realm of trajectory planning predicated upon a model, the transition point exhibits abrupt shifts upon immediate completion of gait transition at a designated juncture. This phenomenon substantially undermines the stability of the robot's ambulation process. This paper undertakes the design of a prototype platform for the KUST-canine quadruped robot by assimilating principles from bionics and mechanical engineering. Focusing on the robot as the subject of inquiry, a methodology involving a compound cycloid foot trajectory is introduced. This methodology introduces a variable control approach during the transition phase, enabling consistent speed and adaptable step length both preceding and following gait transformation. Coalescing ADAMS-Simulink co-simulation experiments with prototype trials, the study attests to the quadruped robot's capacity to traverse steadily in alignment with the proposed algorithm. Evidenced by the ability to seamlessly effect gait transitions, the algorithm's efficacy is firmly established.

articleTitle: A one-class adaptive abnormal state detection method for electromechanical equipment with multi working condition
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The application of data-driven fault diagnosis techniques is becoming increasingly prevalent in the realm of intelligent health management for industrial equipment. These techniques exhibit impressive performance, especially when abundant data samples are available, thanks to the support of deep learning technology. However, gathering and refining training samples pose notable challenges. In practical production scenarios, obtaining comprehensive fault type data remains arduous, whereas normal state data collection is comparatively more feasible. This paper introduces a novel approach to fault diagnosis termed “one-class classification.” This method effectively identifies equipment anomalies using solely normal state data for training. The methodology entails constructing a bi-directional generative adversarial network with dual discriminators. A twice adversarial training strategy is adopted for abnormal state detection. This strategy employs both normal state data and unlabeled test data for supervised and adaptive training, respectively, thereby enhancing the model's generalization capacity. Experimental results substantiate the efficacy of the proposed one-class classification method for fault diagnosis. It demonstrates robust diagnostic accuracy and generalization capability, particularly when discerning abnormalities across diverse domains.

articleTitle: Analysis of the application of RCM maintenance ideas in the operation and maintenance of air traffic control equipment in high altitude airports
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Firstly, it introduces some impact analysis on ATC equipment in the special environment of high plateau airport, followed by the current situation of domestic and international development of the RCM method in the field of aviation and other equipment, which shows that the RCM method is becoming more and more standardized and mature, and has become a mandatory course in the field of equipment maintenance management. Then combined with the current situation of RCM operation and maintenance management research of ATC equipment, the key technologies needed to apply the RCM method to the field of ATC equipment in high plateau airports are analyzed, and finally the application prospects and importance of the RCM method in the operation and maintenance management of ATC equipment in high plateau airports are pointed out.

articleTitle: Maintainability assessment methods for large wind turbines
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The maintainability of wind turbines forms the cornerstone for enhancing operational and maintenance efficiency within wind farms. Strong maintainability constitutes a crucial factor for fostering high-quality advancement in the wind power industry, aligned with the objectives of carbon peak and neutrality. In this paper, the lognormal distribution is used to describe the maintenance time distribution of wind turbines. The goodness of fit test is carried out using the Chi-square distribution to calculate the maintainability characteristic quantity of wind turbines. The point estimation and interval estimation of MTTR, median maintenance time, maximum maintenance time, and maintenance degree at time t are given. The unit faults are divided into five categories, and the influence of unit maintenance time and operation and maintenance support ability of wind farms under different fault categories is discussed.

articleTitle: Bearing cross-domain fault diagnosis based on domain adversarial network
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: A new method has been suggested to tackle the issue of irregularly dispersed bearing vibration data when subjected to varying operational conditions, along with the deficiency of data in the intended domain. This method combines two techniques: the Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) and Domain Adversarial NeuralNetwork (DANN).To begin with, the limited target domain data is fed into the WGAN-GP. This network consists of a generator and a discriminator engaged in a competitive process. The generator's objective is to create synthetic data that bears a strong resemblance to the data in the target domain. In contrast, the discriminator's goal is to differentiate between authentic data from the target domain and the data generated by the generator. Through this adversarial process, the target domain dataset is augmented. The augmented target domain data and source domain data (derived from distinct yet related domain data) are then fed into the DANN. The DANN comprises two components: a label classifier and a domain classifier. The primary role of the label classifier is to detect faults in bearings, whereas the domain classifier endeavors to ascertain whether the data comes from the source domain or the expanded target domain created through augmentation. Through adversarial training between these two classifiers, the network learns to align the data distributions of the two domains. By following this process, the method effectively bridges the distribution gap between the source and target domains. This approach proves capable of accurately diagnosing bearing faults in scenarios where target domain data is scarce. In summary, the proposed methodology employs a combination of WGAN-GP and DANN to enhance the target domain dataset using synthetic data generation and adversarial domain alignment. This approach effectively addresses data distribution disparities between different domains and facilitates accurate bearing fault diagnosis in situations with limited target domain data.

articleTitle: Failure analysis of planetary gear in wind turbine gearbox
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In this article, the chemical composition, microstructure, morphology and micro-component of the fracture are analyzed and tested by chemical composition analysis, metallographic observation, scanning electron microscopy and energy spectrum microcomponent analysis. The results show that the nitrogen content of the planetary wheel is slightly higher than the upper limit, and the local nitrogen content is higher. Improper heat treatment is easy to cause material brittleness, which will significantly reduce the impact toughness of the material. The inner surface of the bearing hole of planetary gear is low in hardness and strength. And it has manufacturing defects and is subject to alternating load, which is easy to cause high cycle fatigue damage of planetary gear. In the process of heat treatment carburizing, the carburizing phenomenon of the lifting hole position of the planetary wheel is not effectively protected, which increases the possibility of micro-cracks in the lifting hole.

articleTitle: Research on the maturity assessment method of intelligent PHM for groundwater circulation well
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: GCW system is one of the hot research objects of in-situ remediation of contaminated groundwater. However, the system will be difficult to maintain if there is a failure during underground operation. The uncertainty of the source of the failure will make it more difficult to perform maintenance on the system, which will delay the remediation process. Therefore, a method that can diagnose or predict system failures in a timely manner is needed. Based on RPL, this study designs an intelligent PHM system to predict potential failures of GCW systems based on the relationship between performance degradation and failure time of GCW systems. And the maturity of the intelligent PHM system is evaluated into 5 levels, and 15 maturity evaluation factors in 4 dimensions are proposed. The maturity model and its application process are obtained. This modeling method provides ideas for decision-makers and managers to carry out early maintenance, and estimate its development level in related fields.

articleTitle: Research on end-to-end fault prediction method of rolling bearing based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In rolling bearing fault prediction, the selection of time-domain and frequency-domain features is often influenced by subjective factors, and the full utilization of time and space features is challenging. To address these issues, a method based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) is proposed. The method involves two main steps. Firstly, a convolutional neural network is used to extract original vibration signal features. A batch regularization layer is added after the convolutional layer to optimize weight and accelerate model training. The efficiency of feature extraction is improved by extending the first convolutional layer and adjusting the step size. Secondly, a bidirectional long-short-term memory neural network is introduced to enhance the utilization of temporal information and extract temporal features. The model's robustness is strengthened through the incorporation of batch regularization layers and dropout layers, reducing data-to-data dependencies. The proposed method is validated using two sets of rolling bearing test data. The results demonstrate the improved fault prediction accuracy compared to traditional methods, along with better performance under different working conditions.

articleTitle: Based on the integration of wind power generators regional wind speed uncertainty analysis
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Wind turbines are devices that convert wind energy into mechanical energy, a process largely governed by the interaction of the wind with the turbine's blades. Accurate recognition of wind characteristics, therefore, forms a vital premise for the effective operation of the wind turbine impeller. The probability distribution of wind speed and direction at specific points within a wind field has substantial implications for turbine location, layout, and fan design, and plays a critical role in the reliability analysis of the system. Since wind speed is subject to a high degree of uncertainty, it constitutes a major factor in assessing the risk of system failure. This uncertainty is influenced by various factors, including temperature, atmospheric pressure, terrain, and geography, all of which contribute to random fluctuations in wind speed. However, despite these uncertainties, the convergence time and spatial characteristics of wind speed do follow certain patterns. Therefore, the establishment of a reliable wind speed model holds significant value for studying the characteristics of wind turbine impellers. Such a model would enable more precise predictions and optimizations, enhancing the overall performance and reliability of wind energy systems.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of reciprocating compressor based on Copula Bayesian Network model
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Due to the complex and nonlinear interdependencies among variables within the reciprocating compressor system (RCS), the incorporation of the Copula function emerges as a viable solution for addressing the intricacies of variable correlation. However, it is important to acknowledge that as the number of variables increases, the dimensionality of the Copula also escalates, consequently leading to augmented computational challenges. This research paper addresses the formidable issues stemming from multifaceted correlations and high-dimensional aspects resultant from numerous variables. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel approach: the Copula Bayesian Network (CBN) model for reliability analysis. This approach amalgamates the Bayesian Network (BN) model with the Copula function. The CBN model excels in conducting probabilistic inference while seamlessly accounting for the intricate correlations between variables. Moreover, it effectively disentangles the composite joint Copula density function (CDF) into localized conditional CDFs. In the subsequent phase, we proceed to construct the CBN model for the RCS and undertake reliability reasoning. Our findings underscore that the reliability of the CBN model is comparatively lower than that of the BN model. This discrepancy accentuates heightened demands in the realm of maintenance and optimization for real-world engineering applications involving the RCS.

articleTitle: Progressive damage model study of wind turbine blade adhesive structure
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: In order to deeply study the fatigue failure process of wind turbine blade adhesive structure, a corresponding theoretical model is constructed to express the process more intuitively and accurately. Based on the fatigue failure mechanism of the adhesive structure, the improved three-dimensional Hashin criterion, the improved Yeh-stratton failure criterion, and the quadratic nominal strain criterion were selected to determine the failure mode at the local failure of the adhesive structure, and the stiffness of the coefficient reduction method and the cohesive model was used to characterize the sudden drop of local stiffness after the failure of the adhesive structure. The fatigue failure process of the structure was compiled into a program using the FORTRAN language and inserted into the ABAQUS software to establish the progressive damage model of the adhesive structure. The fatigue failure process of the adhesive structure of the wind turbine blade I-beam was analyzed by applying the progressive damage model of the adhesive structure, and the results showed that the progressive damage model of the adhesive structure established in this paper could effectively simulate the fatigue failure process of the adhesive structure of the I-beam.

articleTitle: Movement reliability prediction for mechanical products considering the interaction of multiple factors
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Reliability is one of the most important quality characteristics. As a representative of mechanical product performance reliability, movement reliability is influenced by many factors. It illustrates that a certain failure mode is caused by multiple factors. Movement reliability analysis for mechanical products has mostly used the traditional structural decomposition method in the past, namely “Machine-Components-Parts”. It cannot reflect the transfer relationship between relative motion and transmission accuracy. Besides, due to the complex working environment, there are many factors affecting the movement of products, and they are interrelated. Therefore, based on the “Function-Motion-Action” (FMA) method, this paper obtains the reliability prediction for mechanical products by taking the correlation of multiple factors into account. Firstly, the FMA method was used to decompose the whole machine into the smallest action unit-meta-action, of which the movement parameters were used to establish the reliability model. Then, analyze the influencing factors of meta-action movement reliability and the reliability obtained under the multiple factors by using the MC method. Finally, the application and feasibility of the proposed method were illustrated by taking the CNC turntable as the research object. This study has significance for improving the movement reliability of mechanical products.

articleTitle: Investigation of value-of-information method for guiding sensor arrangement in the application of offshore wind turbine blades
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The exploration of marine resources has led to the boom of large-scale offshore constructions. Effective and real-time monitoring and assessment system is thus critical, which is highly correlated with the safe, healthy, and sustainable development of society. With development of monitoring sensing system, a significant amount of sensing data is feasible to be characterized and analyzed. Although infinite information enables to perfect decision-making, the cost of information is not overlooked. The trade-off between the amount and cost of information is one of the dominant and unresolved issues in the system optimization. The objective of this work is to investigate the value-of-information (VoI) concept for optimized scheme of sensors arrangement. A utility function is used to assess the VoI and the cost of information. Kullback-Liebler divergence and inverse cost function are adopted to quantify the values of different sensor configurations, and to consider the manufacturing cost of sensors, respectively. A case study is presented to evaluate the VoI under different sensor placement scenarios. The VoI-analysis-based method shows great potential for assessing the quality of design and supporting optimal engineering decision-making. As an effective method, it possesses significance in rigorously ranking decision alternatives, resulting in rational allocation and efficient utilization of resources.

articleTitle: A review on deep learning in fault analysis of complex systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Complex systems are playing increasingly important roles in the modernization process, so it's necessary to improve their operational reliability. The improvement of system operational reliability can be achieved through faster and more accurate fault diagnosis and prognosis of key components in the system. Traditional machine learning methods and model-based methods have become difficult to effectively diagnose and predict faults, while deep learning, with its excellent data learning ability, has enormous potential in fault diagnosis and prognosis. This paper elaborates on the application research and development of four common deep learning models applied in the fields of fault diagnosis and prognosis: autoencoder and its variants, deep belief network, convolutional neural network and recurrent neural network. The advantages and limitations of various models of deep learning are discussed, and their possible future research directions are prospected.

articleTitle: Improved FMEA method based on TOPSIS
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Based on the improved RPN method, this paper analyzes the reliability of each system of CNC machine tools, studies the fault types, failure modes, and fault causes of each subsystem, and determines its influence on the overall function of the machine tool. Through FMEA analysis and improved subjective and objective data RPN analysis method, the weak position of each system of CNC machine tools is found, the overall impact of each fault on CNC machine tools is understood, and finally, the reliability information of CNC machine tools is obtained. The entropy weight-TOPSIS distance formula is sorted for RPN values, to sort the faults with closer values more accurately, which overcomes the mathematical defects of traditional RPN compared with the traditional RPN method. The research results show that this method can accurately find out the main fault parts of the machine tool, and put forward corresponding preventive measures and solutions for these fault parts, so as to improve the operating life of the machine tool and optimize the performance and reliability of the system. The research results of this paper have important theoretical and practical significance for improving the safety and reliability of CNC machine tool systems.

articleTitle: Emergency material supply in disaster relief operations based on truck-UAV collaborative distribution
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Given the urgency inherent in disaster relief operations, a supply mode for the distribution of emergency materials, utilizing collaboration between truck and drone transportation, is proposed. In this model, decisions concerning the supply method for each depot with specific material demands, the sequential ordering of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and the route planning for the trucks are integrated into a singular combinatorial optimization problem. A mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is formulated to minimize the overall delivery completion time. Two distinct algorithms are devised to solve this problem efficiently: a logic-based Benders decomposition algorithm and a hybrid genetic algorithm. Numerical experiments conducted on 40 instances demonstrate that the proposed model and algorithms robustly support the novel supply mode grounded in truck- UAV collaborative distribution. The results provide valuable insights for decision-makers seeking to develop efficient, accurate, and globally optimal supply solutions and carry significant theoretical and practical implications.

articleTitle: Failure analysis of the subsea wellhead sealing assembly based on the finite element method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: The ring-shaped metal sealing assembly is an important part of the subsea wellhead for offshore oil and gas development. The failure of the sealing assembly may lead to subsea wellhead leaks and blowouts. In order to explore the variation law and failure influencing factors of the ring-shaped metal sealing assembly under different conditions, an approach is presented to analyze the influencing factors of sealing performance based on the metal sealing mechanism and mechanical theory. A finite element model is established for subsea wellhead sealing assembly to explore the mechanical property change law and failure influencing factors of sealing parts under the different conditions of displacement loads and sealing ring flange radius. The results show that when the radius of the flange is 2.55 mm, the minimum average contact stress of the sealing ring material and the maximum average contact stress of the sealed body material meet the sealing conditions and ensure the stability and reliability of the material. When the discharge displacement load is 19.5 mm to 21 mm, the maximum and minimum average contact stresses at the four flanges of the sealing ring meet the sealing conditions. Such a method can provide a reference for the optimization of structural parameters and load parameters.

articleTitle: Research of enterprise development prosperity index based on the industry perspective
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2023)
abstract: Industry risk is one of the non-systematic risks affecting the credit risk of listed companies. At present, most of the listed companies implement diversification strategies, but the existing studies often use a single industry to measure the risk of enterprises, which is not scientific. This study thus endeavors to fill this research gap by using quantitative industry prosperity to study the prosperity of individual enterprises based on a comprehensive consideration of the multiple industries that companies are involved in. This article firstly calculates the industry development prosperity index based on financial indicators, and then quantifies the business of listed companies by industry. After that, we calculate the quantified ratio of each company's business in different industries. Then we calculate the development prosperity index and the excess development index of enterprises. Our research data are obtained from the Wind database, and the indicators related to the company's industry information are calculated from the composition of its main business disclosed. Finally, the empirical analysis of the development index is conducted, and the study shows that the index can provide certain incremental information to predict the future development level of the enterprises more effectively than single industry classification.
